title: With range-wide GBIF temperature indices, communities in 72 networks followed 37%, not 10%, of their spatial temperature gradient in time; marine networks gave most of the change (1948-2025)
abstract: Question: the campaign synthesis sci:sha256:0037934e found that the community temperature index (CTI) of 75 monitoring networks (73 BioTIME 2.0 studies, North American Breeding Bird Survey, UK Butterfly Monitoring Scheme; 1948-2025) followed only 12% of its own spatial CTI-temperature slope over the warming trend and 2% over year-to-year anomalies. It used species temperature indices (STI) from each network's own sites. Does the result hold with range-wide STIs? Method: same networks, sites, temperatures and estimator (rebuild reproduced the published slopes exactly); only the STI changed. External STI = mean 1981-2010 GHCN_CAMS air temperature or HadISST SST of the GBIF occurrence squares of each taxon (13,719 GBIF taxa, plan written before slopes). Comparison on the same taxa; paired network bootstrap; exact split of the internal STI into the part that the external STI predicts and a residual. Results: in 72 networks the pooled slow fraction was 0.098 (95% CI 0.010-0.195) with internal STIs and 0.373 (0.106-0.656) with external STIs; paired difference +0.275 (0.035-0.548). The fast fraction went from 0.025 to 0.111 (difference +0.086, 0.031-0.164). All external variants and a species-only variant agreed. Marine networks caused most of the change (0.22 to 0.86; fast 0.04 to 0.36), and the marine difference stayed with OISST (+0.49, 0.09-0.91). Freshwater went from -0.05 to 0.25 (interval includes 0); terrestrial did not change (0.20 and 0.19). The residual internal-STI part made 59% of the internal spatial slope but followed warming at -0.02; the externally predicted part followed it at 0.27. Conclusion: internal STIs add a steep, static gradient to the spatial benchmark and hide much aquatic, mainly marine, tracking; terrestrial tracking stays weak. Limitations: the gain is a pooled one (58% of networks higher, p = 0.15); all-season GBIF records; GBIF effort bias; surface temperature for marine taxa; genus-level STIs for 23% of labels; associations, not causal effects.
